docs.title: RiotSkillIssue
docs.text:
The production-ready, auto-updating, and fully typed Python wrapper for the Riot Games API.

  • Type-Safe

    100% Pydantic models for all requests and responses. No more dictionary guessing.

  • Auto-Updated

    Generated daily from the Official OpenAPI Spec. Supports LoL, TFT, LoR, and VALORANT.

  • Resilient by Design

    Built-in exponential backoff, circuit breakers, and correct Retry-After handling.

  • Distributed

    Pluggable Redis support for shared rate limiting and caching across multiple processes.

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text: pip install riotskillissue

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        # Look up an account by Riot ID
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.AMERICAS,
            gameName="Faker",
            tagLine="KR1"
        )
        print(f"Found: {account.gameName}#{account.tagLine}")
        print(f"PUUID: {account.puuid}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

API Key Setup

Set the RIOT_API_KEY environment variable, or pass it directly to RiotClient(api_key="..."). Get your key at developer.riotgames.com.

docs.title: Command Line Interface
docs.text: RiotSkillIssue includes a CLI tool for quick lookups and debugging.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The CLI is included with the package:

pip install riotskillissue

For enhanced output formatting, install with dev dependencies:

pip install "riotskillissue[dev]"

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set your API key via environment variable:

export RIOT_API_KEY="RGAPI-your-key-here"

Or pass it directly with --api-key:

riotskillissue-cli summoner "Player#EUW" --api-key "RGAPI-..."

docs.title: live
docs.text:
🎮 Launch an interactive Live Game TUI (Terminal User Interface) that shows real-time information about an ongoing League of Legends match.

riotskillissue-cli live "GameName#TagLine" --region euw1

This is the fastest way to spectate a match from your terminal — one command, instant dashboard.

Arguments:

Argument Description name Riot ID in format GameName#TagLine --region Regional server (default: euw1) --api-key API key (or use RIOT_API_KEY env var) --refresh Auto-refresh interval in seconds (default: 30)

Example:

$ riotskillissue-cli live "Agurin#EUW" --region euw1

This opens a full-screen terminal dashboard showing:

  • Game info — queue type, game duration, platform
  • Blue Team — champions, player names, ranks, win rates, summoner spells
  • Red Team — champions, player names, ranks, win rates, summoner spells
  • Bans — all banned champions

The TUI auto-refreshes every 30 seconds (configurable with --refresh). If the player isn't in a game yet, it will keep checking until one starts.

Keyboard shortcuts:

Key Action R Manual refresh Q / Esc Quit

See the Live Game TUI page for more details and screenshots.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This guide covers all configuration options for the RiotClient.

docs.title: RiotClientConfig
docs.text:
The RiotClientConfig class controls client behavior:

from riotskillissue import RiotClient, RiotClientConfig

config = RiotClientConfig(
    api_key="RGAPI-...",
    max_retries=5,
    connect_timeout=5.0,
    read_timeout=10.0,
)

async with RiotClient(config=config) as client:
    # Use the configured client
    pass

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description api_key str None Your Riot Games API key. Falls back to RIOT_API_KEY env var. max_retries int 3 Maximum retry attempts for failed requests (5xx, network errors). connect_timeout float 5.0 Connection timeout in seconds. read_timeout float 10.0 Read timeout in seconds. redis_url str None Redis URL for distributed rate limiting.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description RIOT_API_KEY Default API key if not provided in config.

docs.title: Redis Integration
docs.text: Enable distributed rate limiting and caching with Redis:

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
For applications running multiple processes or pods:

config = RiotClientConfig(
    api_key="RGAPI-...",
    redis_url="redis://localhost:6379/0"
)

async with RiotClient(config=config) as client:
    # Rate limits are now shared across all instances
    pass

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Reduce API calls with built-in response caching:

from riotskillissue import RiotClient
from riotskillissue.core.cache import RedisCache

cache = RedisCache("redis://localhost:6379/1")

async with RiotClient(cache=cache) as client:
    # First call hits the API
    summoner = await client.summoner.get_by_puuid(
        region="euw1",
        encryptedPUUID="..."
    )

    # Second call returns cached data
    summoner = await client.summoner.get_by_puuid(
        region="euw1",
        encryptedPUUID="..."
    )

docs.title: Retry Behavior
docs.text:
The client automatically retries requests on:

  • HTTP 5xx server errors
  • Network connection failures
  • Rate limit responses (HTTP 429)

Retries use exponential backoff with jitter. For rate limits, the client respects the Retry-After header.

# Customize retry behavior
config = RiotClientConfig(
    api_key="RGAPI-...",
    max_retries=5,  # More retries for unreliable networks
)

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
Configure connection and read timeouts separately:

config = RiotClientConfig(
    api_key="RGAPI-...",
    connect_timeout=3.0,   # Fast fail on connection issues
    read_timeout=30.0,     # Allow slow responses for heavy endpoints
)

docs.title: Loading from Environment
docs.text:
The simplest approach is to use environment variables:

from riotskillissue import RiotClient

# Automatically loads RIOT_API_KEY from environment
async with RiotClient() as client:
    pass

For explicit environment loading:

from riotskillissue import RiotClientConfig

config = RiotClientConfig.from_env()

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will walk you through installing riotskillissue and making your first API call.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • A Riot Games API key from developer.riotgames.com

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package from PyPI:

pip install riotskillissue

For development with testing tools:

pip install "riotskillissue[dev]"

docs.title: Option 1: Environment Variable (Recommended)
docs.text:
Set the RIOT_API_KEY environment variable:

Windows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD)Linux/macOS

docs.title: Your First API Call
docs.text:
Here's a complete example that looks up a player by their Riot ID:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform, Region

async def main():
    # Client auto-loads RIOT_API_KEY from environment
    async with RiotClient() as client:

        # Step 1: Look up account by Riot ID
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,  # Use AMERICAS, EUROPE, ASIA, or SEA
            gameName="Player",
            tagLine="EUW"
        )
        print(f"Account: {account.gameName}#{account.tagLine}")
        print(f"PUUID: {account.puuid}")

        # Step 2: Get summoner data using the PUUID
        summoner = await client.summoner.get_by_puuid(
            region=Region.EUW1,  # Regional server
            encryptedPUUID=account.puuid
        )
        print(f"Summoner Level: {summoner.summonerLevel}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Understanding Regions vs Platforms
docs.text:
The Riot API uses two types of routing:

Type Values Used For Platform AMERICAS, EUROPE, ASIA, SEA Account lookups, Match history Region NA1, EUW1, KR, BR1, etc. Summoner data, Live game, Ranked 
from riotskillissue import Region, Platform

# Platform for account/match APIs
account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
    region=Platform.AMERICAS,
    gameName="Player",
    tagLine="NA1"
)

# Region for summoner/ranked APIs  
summoner = await client.summoner.get_by_puuid(
    region=Region.NA1,
    encryptedPUUID=account.puuid
)

docs.title: Live Game TUI
docs.text: RiotSkillIssue includes a built-in Terminal User Interface (TUI) for spectating live League of Legends matches directly from your terminal. One command gives you a full dashboard with teams, champions, ranks, and more.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
riotskillissue-cli live "Agurin#EUW" --region euw1

That's it. This single command opens an interactive, auto-refreshing dashboard.

docs.title: When a Game is Active
docs.text: The TUI displays a full-screen dashboard with:

docs.title: When Not in a Game
docs.text: If the player isn't currently in a match, the TUI shows a waiting screen and keeps checking:

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Real-time game data — see the current match as it happens
  • Both teams at a glance — champions, summoner spells, ranks, win rates
  • Auto-refresh — data updates every 30 seconds (configurable)
  • Rank colors — each player's rank is color-coded (Iron → Challenger)
  • Win rate highlighting — green for >55%, red for <45%
  • Ban display — all banned champions listed
  • Waiting mode — if the player isn't in a game, the TUI waits and checks periodically
  • Keyboard controls — refresh manually or quit with a single keypress

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The TUI is included with the standard package installation:

pip install riotskillissue

Dependencies

The TUI uses Textual and Rich, which are installed automatically as dependencies.

docs.title: Basic
docs.text:
export RIOT_API_KEY="RGAPI-your-key-here"
riotskillissue-cli live "GameName#TagLine"

docs.title: With Options
docs.text: riotskillissue-cli live "Faker#KR1" --region kr --refresh 15

docs.title: Programmatic Usage
docs.text:
You can also launch the TUI from Python code:

from riotskillissue.tui import run_tui

run_tui(
    api_key="RGAPI-your-key",
    game_name="Agurin",
    tag_line="EUW",
    region="euw1",
    auto_refresh=30,
)

Or use the lower-level app class for more control:

from riotskillissue.tui import LiveGameApp

app = LiveGameApp(
    api_key="RGAPI-your-key",
    game_name="Agurin",
    tag_line="EUW",
    region="euw1",
    auto_refresh=15,
)
app.run()

docs.title: API Key
docs.text:
The TUI requires a valid Riot API key. You can get one from the Riot Developer Portal.

Set it as an environment variable for convenience:

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
export RIOT_API_KEY="RGAPI-your-key-here"

$env:RIOT_API_KEY = "RGAPI-your-key-here"

set RIOT_API_KEY=RGAPI-your-key-here

Development Keys

Riot development API keys expire every 24 hours. For persistent usage, apply for a personal or production key through the Developer Portal.

docs.title: "Not currently in a game"
docs.text: The player must be in an active League of Legends match (loading screen or in-game). Champion select does not count — the Spectator API only reports data once the game has started.

docs.title: "404 - Data not found"
docs.text:
• Double-check the Riot ID spelling and tag line
  • Make sure you're using the correct --region for the player's server
  • Verify your API key is valid and not expired

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: The TUI makes multiple API calls per refresh (spectator + ranks for all 10 players). With a development key (20 requests/second, 100 requests/2 minutes), the default 30-second refresh interval stays well within limits. Lower the interval with caution.

docs.title: Summoner Data
docs.text:
Get summoner profile information:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform, Region

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        # First get the account
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            gameName="Agurin",
            tagLine="EUW"
        )

        # Then get summoner data
        summoner = await client.summoner.get_by_puuid(

if __name__ == "__main__":

docs.title: Match History
docs.text:
Fetch recent matches for a player:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        # Get account
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            gameName="Agurin",
            tagLine="EUW"
        )

        # Get last 5 match IDs
        match_ids = await client.match.get_match_ids_by_puuid(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            puuid=account.puuid,
            count=5
        )

        print(f"Recent matches: {len(match_ids)}")
        for match_id in match_ids:
            print(f"  - {match_id}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Match Details
docs.text:
Get detailed information about a specific match:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        # Get match by ID
        match = await client.match.get_match(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            matchId="EUW1_7654321098"  # Replace with real match ID
        )

        print(f"Game Mode: {match.info.gameMode}")
        print(f"Duration: {match.info.gameDuration // 60} minutes")
        print(f"Queue ID: {match.info.queueId}")

        # Print participants
        print("\nParticipants:")
        for p in match.info.participants:
            kda = f"{p.kills}/{p.deaths}/{p.assists}"
            print(f"  {p.championName}: {p.summonerName} - {kda}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Paginated Match History
docs.text:
Use the pagination helper for large match history fetches:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform, paginate

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            gameName="Agurin",
            tagLine="EUW"
        )

        # Fetch up to 50 matches using pagination
        count = 0
        async for match_id in paginate(
            client.match.get_match_ids_by_puuid,
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            puuid=account.puuid,

docs.title: TFT Match Details
docs.text:
Get detailed information about a TFT match:

import asyncio
from riotskillissue import RiotClient, Platform

async def main():
    async with RiotClient() as client:
        account = await client.account.get_by_riot_id(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            gameName="Player",
            tagLine="EUW"
        )

        # Get most recent match
        match_ids = await client.tft_match.get_match_ids_by_puuid(
            region=Platform.EUROPE,
            puuid=account.puuid,
            count=1
        )

        if match_ids:
            match = await client.tft_match.get_match(
                region=Platform.EUROPE,
                matchId=match_ids[0]
            )

            print(f"Game Version: {match.info.game_version}")
            print(f"Queue ID: {match.info.queue_id}")

            # Find our player in the match
            for participant in match.info.participants:
                if participant.puuid == account.puuid:
                    print(f"\nYour placement: {participant.placement}")
                    print(f"Level: {participant.level}")
                    print(f"Gold left: {participant.gold_left}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
